unit: Kodak Pakon F-135 Plus, owner's unit (U34 repaired 2026-08-06)

config.duty_note: Flat field captured at open-gate duty [462,231,98], searched so the MAXIMUM lands on the vendor 64000 target (measured 61666/62715/62310, zero clipped). Scanning uses with-film = open-gate x 10^D (R 1.393157 / G 2.511891 / B 5.188016), the colour-negative base density, exactly as FN_bBeforeScan selects DutyCycle_* over DutyCycleOpenGate_*. The vendor stored duties for this unit ([702,371,158] open-gate) clipped 97 percent of an empty gate on this hardware -- its LEDs read well below their 2022 values -- so the vendor METHOD was applied rather than its stored numbers.

config_source: read from the captures' own sidecars (flat_dark_01.bin.scan.json and flat_bright_01.bin.scan.json), which agreed on every key in ['integration_0x82_idx6', 'lamp_pwm_N', 'line_rate_0x91', 'levels_R_G_B_Ir', 'on_counts_R_G_B', 'afe_gains', 'afe_offsets', 'fpga_ctrl', 'pixel_offset', 'pixel_height', 'dpi_base']. NOT copied from a previous calibration/README.json — these tables are valid for the setup the captures were actually taken under and nothing else.

dark_source.note: black level, empty gate, lamp off. Target band 400..4000 wire counts; a reference sitting on ADC code 0 is refused, because a clipped pedestal loses everything below it and cannot be corrected afterwards (docs/72). The AFE offsets that produce it are recorded in config.afe_offsets and are a per-DPI-base calibration output, not a constant.

bright_source.note: empty gate, lamp on, unclipped: peak 63554 of 65535 wire full scale. Target was 64000 on the 'max' statistic (the vendor's FN_bCalibrateFindLedCurrent target is 64000, and docs/15 records that its check compares the MAXIMUM pixel of an averaged CCD line, not the mean); measured level 57401. This unit's brightest sample sits 1.1072x its level, so the highest clip-free level here is about 58287.

usage: Tables are EP 0x86 wire u16. Decode: dark14=dark/4; (raw14-dark14)*gain → clamp 14-bit. Gate uses wire as-is.
formula: dark = mean down the strip; gain[:,c] = (bright-dark)[:,c].mean() / (bright-dark)[:,c] — normalised PER CHANNEL, not globally
